brief: Premium yoga and studio-to-street apparel. $80-130 per piece. Celebrity-adjacent aesthetic, so we want shoppers who care about brand and wellness.

profile.business_summary: Premium yoga and studio-to-street apparel brand featuring a celebrity-adjacent aesthetic, targeting brand-conscious and wellness-focused shoppers with products priced between $80 and $130 per piece.

relevant_tags.why: Core product category is activewear/studio-to-street apparel.
Core product category is yoga apparel.
Studio-to-street apparel is adjacent to casual wear.
The brand targets shoppers who care about wellness.
Shoppers taking fitness classes are highly likely to purchase premium yoga apparel.

persona_conflicts.evidence: Advertiser claims a 'celebrity-adjacent aesthetic' which strongly aligns with influencer positioning.

persona_conflicts.conflict: disinterested_in: luxury-only messaging, vague premium positioning
persona_conflicts.evidence: Advertiser positions itself as premium ($80-130 per piece) with a celebrity-adjacent aesthetic.

note_signals.why: Movewell has fitness-engaged shoppers with strong crossover in wellness and beauty, matching the target audience perfectly.
Studiogrid users are actively spending on self-care and fitness, making them prime candidates for premium yoga wear.
Linden Park has a conservative brand sensibility, which conflicts with the advertiser's celebrity-adjacent aesthetic.
Velvetline features a minimalist aesthetic and identity-driven purchasing, aligning well with brand-conscious, celebrity-adjacent shoppers.

profile.gate_reason: The product, price point, and target audience are clearly defined, allowing for immediate planning and matching.

config.advertiser_summary: Premium yoga and studio-to-street apparel brand featuring a celebrity-adjacent aesthetic, targeting brand-conscious and wellness-focused shoppers with products priced between $80 and $130 per piece.

assumptions: No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 60% gross margin (typical for apparel). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($105 x 60% margin x 1.1 orders = $69.30).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $48.51 x click-to-purchase rate (1.0%-3.5% for apparel). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.28 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.36 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.27 -> relative fit x1.36 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.32 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.26 -> relative fit x1.35 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.31 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%; host sells a competing product, so it may decline (capacity discounted)
score 0.24 -> relative fit x1.28 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.24 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%; host sells a competing product, so it may decline (capacity discounted)

warnings: No budget given: recommending $2,710, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $48.51 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
